messages:
julia: noticed a sudden run of ClusterRoleBinding creations coming from CI runners after the kubelet cert rotation, suspicious.
sec-bot: automated alert: anomalous RBAC write activity detected for system:serviceaccount:ci:runner-sa at 2026-02-27T14:03:21Z
amanda: can you paste the kube audit line?
julia: pasted (redacted):

"timestamp":"2026-02-27T14:03:21Z", "user":"system:serviceaccount:ci:runner-sa", "verb":"create", "resource":"clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io", "objectRef":{"name":"ci-runner-clusterbind"}

mike: looks like a post-install job in the ci-runner chart is running in-cluster as runner-sa and doing `kubectl create clusterrolebinding`.
vikram: that would explain it. chart change repointed a hook to run as a pod instead of via deploy controller.
amanda: immediate mitigation: remove clusterbinds and replace with namespace-scoped Roles. we should also prevent jobs from holding cluster-level rights.
julia: proposed quick fix: create ci-runner-deployer SA scoped to target namespaces and update pipeline to impersonate it. delete the cluster-level binding after staging validation.
sec-bot: policy note: in-cluster RBAC management must be explicitly approved. add annotation `infra.security/allow-rbac-change: "true"` and require a security ticket.
ops: can someone paste a minimal Role/RoleBinding we can apply in staging?
mike: posting minimal example to apply into target-ns (staging):

```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: ci-deployer
  namespace: target-ns
rules:
- apiGroups: ["apps"]
  resources: ["deployments"]
  verbs: ["get","list","create","update","patch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-deployer-binding
  namespace: target-ns
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: ci-runner-deploy
  namespace: ci
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: ci-deployer
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

amanda: KMS concern: current key policy lets the CI job decrypt tokens for any namespace. I will scope KMS decrypt with condition `kms:RequestTag/namespace = ci` and require `kms:CallerAccount` match and short TTL.
vikram: also suggest adding `kms:EncryptionContext:namespace` check so keys can't be used cross-namespace.
julia: longer plan bullet list:
- introduce `ci-runner-deploy` SA, update pipeline to impersonate it (staging rollout)
- remove ClusterRoleBindings referencing runner-sa after canary
- tighten KMS key policy to namespace-tag + TTL <= 5m
- add chart linter rule to fail PRs that add cluster-scoped RBAC objects
- add nightly RBAC drift job to alert on new clusterrolebindings from non-admin charts
- require manual sec approval for any chart hook that manipulates RBAC

mike: opened PR for role + pipeline impersonation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/128
amanda: opened infra PR for KMS policy change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/342
vikram: I'll add the chart linter rule and a failing test in charts-ci.
ops: oncall tagged: @oncall-eng - if a deploy breaks due to missing perms we need an emergency rollback path. we should be able to temporarily rebind the old cluster role with a short TTL via a puerta job.
oncall-eng: acknowledged. will prepare a rollback playbook and a one-click rebind runbook.
julia: tested in staging: when clusterrolebinding removed, old runner-sa causes 403s and logs show attempted `create clusterrolebinding`, while impersonated `ci-runner-deploy` can create deployments in target ns successfully. audit shows user=ci-runner-deploy for create deployment events. :white_check_mark:
amanda: scheduling clusterbind removal during 02:00Z low traffic window after KMS PR merges and monitoring configured.
sec-bot: checklist for removal: (1) KMS policy merged, (2) role/rolebinding PR merged and deployed to staging, (3) chart linter active, (4) canary monitoring enabled. auto-approve conditionally.
julia: will write a short incident trace once cleanup completes and any lessons learned.
ops: moving to action; will watch prom alerts for RBACChange and KMS decrypt spikes. thanks team.
